@graph.headline: How to Clean a Wood Fence in Michigan: Leaf Stains, Green Algae, Mildew, and the Gray That Isn't Dirt

mainEntity.name: How do I get green algae off a wood fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oxygen bleach (sodium percarbonate), applied bottom to top to already-wet wood, left to dwell three to five minutes, scrubbed with a soft nylon brush, and rinsed with a garden hose or very low pressure. Chlorine bleach also kills algae but attacks lignin and fuzzes the wood, so it is the wrong tool for cedar.

mainEntity.name: Can I pressure wash a cedar fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, carefully. Stay in the 500–800 PSI range on cedar, use a 40-degree fan tip, hold the wand 12–18 inches from the boards, and work with the grain. If the surface starts to look fuzzy, stop — you are removing wood fiber, not dirt. Never use a 0-degree tip on a wood fence.

mainEntity.name: What is the gray on my old wood fence — is it dirt?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Gray on unfinished wood is UV-degraded lignin with fungal growth feeding on it. Cleaning removes the growth, and an oxalic acid brightener restores some color, but heavy gray with a rough, hairy surface means the outer fibers are gone and cannot be washed back.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove leaf stains from a wood fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Leaf stains are tannin stains. Soap will not lift them. Apply an oxalic acid wood brightener to a damp surface, let it sit about fifteen minutes, and rinse. Heavier stains take a second application. Clear the leaves first, or the stain will simply come back with the next rain.

mainEntity.name: Is it too late to clean and seal my fence in November in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cleaning is fine as long as air temperatures stay above about 40°F and no hard freeze is coming. Sealing is usually not: most stains need 50°F or warmer, some oil-based products go down to 35–40°F, and wood must be at 12 percent moisture content or below. Cleaning now and finishing in April is the better play.

mainEntity.name: Will cleaning make a 15-year-old fence look new again?

acceptedAnswer.text: It will look considerably better — growth gone, tannins lifted, some color restored. It will not look new. Weathering changes the wood itself, and once the outer fibers are worn away no cleaner brings them back. Cleaning buys appearance and time; it does not reverse age.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to have a fence cleaned in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Professional cleaning typically runs about $1.50–$3.50 per linear foot for a single side, with most contractors carrying a minimum charge. DIY is usually $40–$90 in materials for a 150-foot run plus a pressure washer rental. Brightening and staining are priced separately.

mainEntity.name: Should I clean both sides of the fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually yes, if you have access. Mildew grows through board gaps, the shaded side ages the sunny side, and a fence cleaned on one face only tends to look worse, not better. If access requires a neighbor's permission, ask before you start — and cover their plantings if you are spraying.
